result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, with a wider walkway and mature trees on the left. However, the environment lacks high-visibility crossing infrastructure and is characterized by significant visual obstructions from on-street parallel parking.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street obscures sightlines between pedestrians (especially children) and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the block

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The visible crosswalk markings in the foreground are significantly faded, reducing their effectiveness in alerting drivers to pedestrian presence.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace faded markings with continental or ladder-style high-visibility paint to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond parked cars.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove the parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

result.summary: The environment is a narrow, one-way residential street with row houses built directly to the sidewalk edge. While the narrow roadway naturally limits vehicle speeds, the pedestrian experience is hampered by narrow sidewalks obstructed by utility poles and a lack of modern crossing infrastructure like curb ramps or high-visibility markings.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street limits visibility between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles and building steps encroach on the already narrow walking path.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The existing crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Daylighting)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to prevent parking near the crosswalk, improving sightlines and shortening the crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk using a high-visibility continental pattern to increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and proper slopes at the crossing point to ensure accessibility for all users.

result.summary: A narrow residential street lined with row houses and parallel parked cars on both sides. Sidewalks are present and continuous, though relatively narrow, and a curb ramp with a tactile warning pad is visible at the nearest corner.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars along both sides of the narrow street block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers, especially near the corner.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the street view.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalks
hazards.description: Despite the presence of a curb ramp, there are no painted crosswalk markings to designate a safe crossing point.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corner in the foreground.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corner to shorten the crossing distance and prevent cars from parking too close to the intersection.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a narrow residential street with sidewalks on both sides and a modern curb ramp with tactile warnings on the right corner. While the low-speed nature of the street is beneficial, the lack of marked crosswalks and visual obstructions from parked cars near the intersection present safety risks.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: The intersection lacks painted crosswalks, which reduces driver awareness of potential pedestrian crossings.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the corner block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the intersection

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: Potholes and uneven pavement in the roadway near the curb ramp could cause tripping or difficulty for mobility devices.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian paths and improve driver yielding.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Pavement Repair
interventions.description: Resurface the roadway near the intersection to eliminate tripping hazards and improve accessibility.
